summary: Answered the owner's two notes on Disaster Desk's Texas City long video: long titles must now name the event as people search it, and an event's thumbnail must show the event, not a gauge, both checked in code for every channel. The fact reviewer now uses the archived CIA World Factbook. No Shorts challenger started yet: too little data.
why: Owner notes come first (two open on L-20261122-42: title and thumbnail too technical). One adopt proposal (factbook-retired) was a plain fix. No experiment is running on any channel and Shorts with 48 h data are 6, 3, 2 and 0, too few to start a weekly-loop cycle; the 21 Nov owner changes still need their first Shorts read.

findings.title: Texas City long video: title and thumbnail only made sense to someone who knew the story
findings.detail: Topic title 'The Gauge Said Normal. The Tower Was Nearly Full.', video title 'How BP's Texas City Refinery Blew Up While Its Gauge Read Normal' (no 'explosion'), thumbnail A a green NORMAL panel beside a red tank with 'It was full'. The topic's top hit (2.26M views) shows the geyser over the refinery.

findings.title: Evaluator: no experiments running on any channel
findings.detail: Geography 6 Shorts with 48 h data (why_shaped 79.3% viewed vs what_if_world 58.7%), tech 3 (45.5% viewed), Craze & Crash 2, Disaster Desk 0. Impact: geography's week of 16 Nov n=3, 737 median views, 62.8% viewed, 59.2% stayed to watch.

findings.title: Recurring failures are mostly notes the checks already explain
findings.detail: Top kinds in 14 days: text off the frame (geography 11 videos), gaps with nothing new (tech 6), the story spine (Craze & Crash 13), source lines too wide (Disaster Desk 4); each check's message already says the fix.
